stem: A manufacturing study measures defect rate across 4 factorys, each containing multiple production lines. factory A has 8 observations with mean 66.8 % (within-factory SD = 3.2). factory B has 10 observations with mean 56.7 % (within-factory SD = 4.9). factory C has 8 observations with mean 56.3 % (within-factory SD = 6.1). factory D has 8 observations with mean 74.2 % (within-factory SD = 9.8). The between-factory standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 7.4 and 18.5 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true defect rate for factory D, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-factory variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for factory D: 73.4 % (shrunk from raw 74.2). Range [72.2, 73.8] as between-factory SD varies from 7.4 to 18.5. Pooled mean: 63.1.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 63.1 % (weighted average of 4 factory means).
Shrinkage factor for factory D: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=12.3: B = 0.926.
Interval [72.2, 73.8] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (74.2) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (63.1) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
